title: Parity indices (female/male, rural/urban, bottom/top wealth quintile)
graph_title: Parity indices (female/male, rural/urban, bottom/top wealth quintile)
national_indicator_available: Parity indices (female/male, rural/urban, bottom/top wealth quintile)
national_indicator_description: These indicators measure the gap between female and male, rural and urban, and bottom and top wealth quintiles with respect to a range of education indicators. A value of 1 indicates parity between the two groups.
computation_definitions:
Several parity indices are included in this indicator.

- Gender parity index, Participation rate of youth in formal and non-formal education and training

- Gender parity index, Computer literacy rate

- Gender parity index, Learners who meet benchmark in Kinyarwanda reading, English reading, and mathematics

- Rural-to-urban parity index, Learners who meet benchmark in English reading and mathematics

- Gender parity index, Teachers with the minimum required qualifications

- Gender parity index, Participation rate in organized learning (one year before the official primary entry age)

- Gender parity index, Gross intake rate in final year (primary, lower secondary, and upper secondary education)

- Gender parity index, Literacy rate

- Rural-to-urban parity index, Literacy rate

- Wealth parity index, Literacy rate
computation_calculations:
Gender parity index (GPI) = (Rate among females) / (Rate among males)

Rural-to-urban parity index = (Rate among rural residents) / (Rate among urban residents)

Wealth parity index = (Rate among bottom consumption quintile) / (Rate among top consumption quintile)
other_info: Some additional information on gender, urban/rural, wealth, location, and disability gaps is available in the linked data sources.
comments_limitations: The list of parity indices provided here is a subset of the list recommended in the global metadata due to data availability. Please see the linked data source for additional information on methodology and limitations.
indicator_name: Parity indices (female/male, rural/urban, bottom/top wealth quintile and others such as disability status, indigenous peoples and conflict-affected, as data become available) for all education indicators on this list that can be disaggregated
target_name: By 2030, eliminate gender disparities in education and ensure equal access to all levels of education and vocational training for the vulnerable, including persons with disabilities, indigenous peoples and children in vulnerable situations
indicator_definition: Parity indices require data for the specific groups of interest. They represent the ratio of the indicator value for one group to that of the other. Typically, the likely more disadvantaged group is placed in the numerator. A value of exactly 1 indicates parity between the two groups.
un_custodian_agency: United Nations Education and Scientific Cultural Organisation - Institute for Statistics (UNESCO-UIS)

source_other_info_1: This is the data source used for indices relating to (a) Participation rate of youth in formal and non-formal education and training; (b) Teachers with the minimum required qualifications; (c) Participation rate in organized learning (one year before the official primary entry age); and (d) Gross intake rate in final year of education. Some additional information on gender and disability gaps is available in the reports.
source_organisation_2: National Institute of Statistics of Rwanda (NISR)
source_other_info_2: This is the data source used for indices relating to (a) Computer literacy rate and (b) Literacy rate. Some additional information on gender, urban/rural, location, and wealth gaps is available in the reports.
source_organisation_3: National Examination and School Inspection Authority (NESA)
source_other_info_3: This is the data source used for indices relating to learners who meet benchmark in Kinyarwanda reading, English reading, and mathematics. Gender and urban/rural parity information is not reported consistently across the different iterations of LARS. Some additional information on gender, urban/rural, and disability performance gaps is available in the reports. Figures from LARS I (2011), LARS II (2014), and LARS III (2017) can be found on page 89 of the April 2019 [Summative GPE country program evaluation](https://www.globalpartnership.org/node/document/download?file=document/file/2019-07-summative-gpe-country-program-evaluation-rwanda.pdf) for Rwanda. Figures from the most recent LARS surveys can be found in the [LARS 2021 Executive Summary Report](https://www.nesa.gov.rw/fileadmin/user_upload/NESA/Ressources/Reports/LARS_2021_EXECUTIVE_SUMMARY.pdf), the [LARS 2023 Reports](https://www.nesa.gov.rw/1/resources?tx_filelist_filelist%5Baction%5D=list&tx_filelist_filelist%5Bcontroller%5D=File&tx_filelist_filelist%5Bpath%5D=%2Fuser_upload%2FNESA%2FRessources%2FLARS_2023%2F&cHash=e27e5b3c9afa337d5c43eb59852fefeb), and the [LARS 2025 Report](https://www.nesa.gov.rw/fileadmin/user_upload/NESA/Ressources/LARS_2025_REPORT/LARS_2025_REPORT.pdf).
